title: WIRED's AI clones copied colleagues and exposed the cost
teaser: A WIRED journalist at Condé Nast built AI versions of his editors, Brian Barrett and Sophie Kleinman, using Gemini and fragments of their working lives. The experiment was meant to test whether digital colleagues could help him understand editorial preferences, prepare ideas and reduce the need to interrupt real people. Instead, the bots became convincing enough to unsettle their originals while remaining too repetitive, error-prone and synthetic to replace them. The result is a useful warning about workplace AI: imitation can make a system feel personal without giving it the judgment that makes a colleague valuable.
